title: Lomagundi–Jatuli carbon isotope excursion
summary: Between about 2.3 and 2.1 billion years ago marine carbonates record the Lomagundi–Jatuli Event, described as the largest positive carbon-isotope excursion in Earth history in both amplitude and duration. Its timing is disputed: one review brackets its duration between 128 and 249 million years, and a 2026 Bayesian analysis puts the onset at 2,445 Ma. It is discussed alongside Earth's oxygenation.

uncertainty.note: Range follows Prave et al. (2021), "between 2.3–2.1 Ga". Martin et al. (2013) bracket it between 2221 ± 5 to 2106 ± 8 Ma (minimum) and 2306 ± 9 to 2057 ± 1 Ma (maximum) if synchronous; Edmonsond and Dyer (2026) give 2,445 to 2,018 Ma. The id uses 2220 Ma. Years are Ga with no 1950 offset.

where.modern_name: Global signal in marine carbonates; pin at Karelia, NW Russia (Wikidata point), where Prave et al. measured LJE-bearing successions

paleo.not_applicable: Age is beyond the 1000 Ma limit of the MERDITH2021 plate model.

importance.justification: The largest recorded carbonate carbon-isotope excursion, linked in the literature to Earth's oxygenation.
